TCP delivers an ordered byte stream and retransmits unacknowledged data. HTTP uses that stream to send page requests and responses.

The sequence number locates bytes in the stream. ACK indicates the next byte the receiver expects.
Number of bytes the receiver advertises it can accept; it differs from the sender's congestion window.
